episodes.title: Queen Sunduk
episodes.verdict: Rebuild the front door around Sunduk: introduce her first, put 'Ridiculous' and the crowning on the page, and cut the cast to about six names so the Yushin romance and the 'king for all' vow can land.
episodes.romance: The best writing in the episode, and it is played, not told: the maids' chorus [43]–[44], her blush at his bare back [45], 'Look at me. Not the door.', then 'Once.' / 'Once what.' / '…Yushin-ah.' [53]–[56], and her choice to shut the door: 'So from now on — «Your Majesty». Nothing else.' [60]. Desire, an obstacle and a costly choice are all there, and [57] (he will still hear it on the day he dies) is a perfect future-told-as-memory. What's missing: we have known both of them for minutes, so there is little to lose; his feeling is told at [39] ('everyone notices'); the obstacle (why a queen can't have him) is only implied by [58]; and the 612 flashback interrupts at the peak. One earlier exchange where the pull is visible (expand [33]–[34]) would make [60] hurt. The thread then goes dark until #13.
episodes.best: '…Once.' / 'Once what.' / 'Call me by name, not by title.' / '…Yushin-ah.' [53]–[56]
episodes.worst: [23]–[40]: the crowning, the main event, is one sentence [35] inside a lecture, a quote, an office table and two cards.
fixes: Start with Sunduk and make 'Ridiculous' a scene: she is being dressed while an elder outside the screen says it, and she answers. Crown her on the page in three lines instead of [35]'s summary.

Cut the cast to about six names (Sunduk, Yushin, Chunchu, Munhee, Bupmin, the Second Emperor): drop Inmun [4], the colour glosses [26], Euljé and the table [38], Pumsuk [62], the market woman and Cheomseongdae [66]–[68], Wu [75], Youngryu and Jomei [73]–[83].
Plant the book's two engines clearly: move the 612 vow [47] onto the hill scene [10]–[14], and card the Second Emperor at [75] as the emperor of Tang.

episodes.title: Harmony Council
episodes.verdict: Spend the words on the argument, not the rules: tell the unanimity rule once, then dramatize the 'no' votes turning, which now happens off-page between [22] and [27].
episodes.best: Kim Yongsu: 'That room eats the men who amuse it.' … 'Wherever the room has to come to you.' [14.4]–[14.6]
episodes.worst: [6]–[11]: the same rule and the same 3–3 count, told by narrator, record, diagram and character in a row.
fixes: Cut the rule's repeats ([7], [8], [10], [11]) and spend the space on the flip: let Suljong, the one named holdout, move his piece on the page after Alchun's tiger line.
Fix the cast: name only the holdout and Alchun, settle whether Yushin votes, and tie Chunchu's royal mother to #1's 'Chunmyung'.
Open on the logline line, and give Kim Yongsu's motto a present-day echo (Chunchu waiting outside, letting the room come to him) so the best plant in the episode has somewhere to go.

episodes.title: Jinheung, the Cloud
episodes.verdict: Turn the biography into one scene (the old men after the wine could carry it all) or fold it into #2 as a short flashback; as written it's a wiki page with a great first line.
episodes.battle: No battle on the page. Jinheung's conquests are one sentence [2], and the betrayal 'afternoon' at Gwansan is deliberately withheld (it opens at #20). Fine as a tease, but nothing replaces it: the episode has no conflict at all.
episodes.best: 'A cloud never asks whose field it's raining on.' [18]
episodes.worst: [7]–[12]: a long stele quote, the Hwarang explained twice and a second quote, with no person in sight.
fixes: Give it a scene: let the old men 'after the wine' [14]–[18] carry the whole episode, with the stones, the yard and the monk's robe told as their gossip.
Cut the Hwarang annal quote [12] and the two unknown names in [11].
Or fold the episode into #2 as a five-block flashback when someone mentions the old king's yard.

episodes.title: Prince Euija
episodes.verdict: The model: leave it alone. The one fix belongs outside it, honouring the Silla grudge the previous card promised.
episodes.romance: Not a romance, but the Euija–Gyebek bond does a romance's work: a want, an obstacle, a rescue, and a choice that costs something ('Do you like the name, or do you like me?' [111.8]).
episodes.best: 'How many times have you gone in?' 'Nineteen.' … 'At twenty I would not come back out.' [67]–[70]
episodes.worst: Barely anything: [116]'s montage recaps lines from minutes earlier, a manhwa habit that prose readers may skim.
fixes: No changes inside the episode beyond the one Silla line in [14]–[18], so #3's card is honoured and Baekje's pilot touches Silla's.
Optional: trim the [116] recap montage.

episodes.title: Eight Great Clans
episodes.verdict: Open on the sand and dramatize Gyebek vs the Jinmo boy with Euija watching; cut the nine term cards to one and fold the clan fighting styles into the bouts.
episodes.battle: The clan tournament is the slice's only on-page fighting. The sword bout [18]–[19] and the Hae–Guk throw [21] have good physical detail ('the way a dock goes quiet when a rope snaps'), but nobody we know is fighting and the scoring is opaque ('Point to the white sleeve', when every fighter wears white). The one bout with stakes, Gyebek against a boy who threatened his life in #4 [50], is summarized at [24]. Dramatize that one and cut the others to a line each.
episodes.best: 'Nobody alive can say what started it. Everybody alive can list the last six things.' [41]
episodes.worst: [2]–[11]: a quote plus nine term cards straight after the book's best episode, before a single scene; and Euija, the hero of #4, has no lines in the whole episode.
fixes: Open at [13] on the sand and make Gyebek vs the Jinmo boy [24] a full scene with Euija reacting (and speaking). It's the payoff #4 promised.
Cut [2], [4]–[7], [9], [11], [28]–[33] and [36]; fold the Hae and Guk styles into the bouts.
Fix the logic slips: the taunts after a Hae–Guk bout [22]–[23], 'the white sleeve' [19], the levy anecdote [52]. Plant the Eraha chant before the card uses it.

episodes.title: Gunchogo, the 13th
episodes.verdict: Either dramatize the king dying on his own wall (one Goguryeo soldier's eyes, one arrow) or fold the episode into #5 as two paragraphs; two annal entries of the same death are not an episode.
episodes.battle: A king killed by a stray arrow on his own wall is a great battle image, and it is told only as two annal entries [3]–[4]. No POV, no geography, no plan, no reversal, no cost felt by anyone. If the episode stays, give it one person on that wall.
episodes.best: 'It is the sentence that gets Daeya burned.' [9]
episodes.worst: [3]–[7]: three quotes in five blocks, two of them telling the same death.
fixes: Fold into #5's ending as a two-paragraph flashback (the chant, the king on his wall, 'Goguryeo remembers it too'), or dramatize the wall from one Goguryeo soldier's eyes.
Cut quotes [3] and [7]; gloss 'Eraha' once; settle the spelling of the king's name.
Change the card's 'Back to the snow' to 'North, to the snow'.

episodes.title: Commander Yeon
episodes.verdict: Strong character, muddled first half: open on the logline, run the traitor interrogation once and in order, and cut two of the three wall records.
episodes.best: 'Where do you think that boy is standing when he is grown.' … 'That is why I am taking him.' [26]–[28]
episodes.worst: [4]–[13]: the execution, rumours, three records, then the same interrogation again, out of order.
fixes: Open on 'Everyone in the north has a story about the Eternal General. None of them are bedtime stories.' and run the interrogation once: [4], then [11]–[13], then [5].
Cut quotes [9]–[10] and two of the three Gulgul cards; keep one epithet.
Tie the Tang at [8] to the emperor who mocked Silla's queen in #1, so the third pilot touches the first.

episodes.title: High Summit
episodes.verdict: Give the summit two faces instead of four position papers, call back 'say half', and cut the epitaph and the art-direction narration from the birth scene.
episodes.romance: Not a romance. Yeon's wife has no name and one line [38], so the birth plays as Yeon's beat, not hers.
episodes.best: Yeon Gusesa, almost kindly: 'Nephew. Sit down. The Summit does not run on prophecies.' [26]
episodes.worst: [3]–[15]: an explainer stack, then interchangeable commanders reading out budgets, with five battle names in one line.
fixes: Cut [4], [6], [7] and give the room two faces: the uncle (planted in #7) and the southern commander who has fought Yushin. Fold the north and west asks into one line.
Call back 'half' after the walkout (Dosuryu: 'That was half?'), and let the narrator wink once at the king's 'King for All' [9]: he isn't the first man this year to say it.
In the birth scene, cut the art direction in [37], plant the Samsin painting, fix night vs daylight, and cut the epitaph [44].

episodes.title: Gwanggaeto, the Great King
episodes.verdict: Its one big idea (Silla knows the price of foreign help, and a Silla prince will ask for it again [9]) should be the card and the bridge into #10. The rest repeats itself in 276 words.
episodes.battle: Fifty thousand horsemen clear a capital of invaders in one clause [0], told again in [5]. No POV, no geography, no fight. The episode rightly cares about the price after the battle, but it needs one human face: the begging Silla king, or a hostage prince riding north.
episodes.best: 'Silla had asked. That's the part everyone forgets.' [5]
episodes.worst: [2]–[4]: the same fortress count twice and a map card in a 276-word episode.
fixes: Fold into #8's ending or #10's start as a short flashback, or keep it and dramatize one moment: the Silla king's plea, or a Silla hostage prince riding north.
Rewrite the card around [9]: the Silla prince who will one day beg an emperor has a son, and the son is fifteen.
Cut [3] and the stele quote [10].

episodes.title: Bupmin
episodes.verdict: An establishing episode with no scene in it: cut the club and principle widgets to one each, and give Bupmin a ride he fails so Yushin’s question lands on something we saw.
episodes.best: “A king for all who cannot hold a saddle is a poem, not a country.” [13]
episodes.worst: [17]–[27]: the Five Principles in five formats back to back, one of them untranslated Korean, with no scene around them.
fixes: Open on [4]’s line, then dramatize a ride (Bupmin and Gotaso racing; he pulls up, she doesn’t) so [28] answers something we watched.
Collapse [17]–[24] into [26]–[27]; cut or translate the Korean VERSE [19].
Cut [9]–[12] to one club joke and drop the Radiance/Yellow Mountain lecture at [16].

episodes.title: Sadaham
episodes.verdict: The best episode in the slice, near Prince Euija level; trim the two battle records and the Council lecture so the fast lands clean.
episodes.romance: Not a romance, but the slice’s best-played love story. It has shared shorthand from the first line (who snores), an object that carries the feeling (the grey stone, pushed across the mat at [20.8]), a vow that costs everything, and a payoff in five words (“…Wait up. / I’m not late.” [21.4]). Measure the two romances that follow against it.
episodes.battle: The Gaya campaign is skipped on purpose (“Any old man in the market will give you the gate” [14]). That works because the frame tells you why. The captives beat at [17] does the battle’s character work better than a charge would.
episodes.best: “…Wait up. / I’m not late.” [21.4]
episodes.worst: [15]–[16] and [24]: records and a lecture right where the frame has promised the opposite.
fixes: Cut the Nihon Shoki quote [16] and Yushin’s Council line [24].
Trim the OATH widget [9.11] to its first lines.
Leave the rest alone; this is the template for the arc.

episodes.title: Gotaso
episodes.verdict: A gripping prologue and a vivid heroine paired with a blank hero: tie the abduction to the romance and give Pumsuk one line that shows who he is.
episodes.romance: Desire is loud and fun, all on Gotaso’s side (“I already did. And he looked back. He did, he did.” [34]), and Munhee’s “Sixteen years old, using the word life” [36] is good banter. Escalation is a clean ladder: glance [30], daily meetings [43], hand [45], rain [48]–[57]. But there is no obstacle on the page (no rank bar, no rival; the frightening father exists only in the card), no choice that costs anything, and Pumsuk has no voice. The four-named-children joke [54]–[57] is charming. We root for her, not for them.
episodes.best: “Father… there is something on your coat.” / “So there is. / I will change it later.” [18]–[19]
episodes.worst: [39]–[46]: the flowering-trees exchange is all pauses, with nobody home on his side.
fixes: Fix [1] so the abduction reads as why her father will demand a vow, not as where the romance ‘begins’; bridge [24]→[25] with one line of aftermath.
Give Pumsuk a voice in [42]–[46]: one boast, one risk, one thing only he would say.
Cut [6] and [50]; make Gotaso 14 at [3].

episodes.title: Pumsuk
episodes.verdict: The episode belongs to Sunduk and Yushin: play the father’s vow as a full scene and cut the lantern-sellers and Haesang.
episodes.romance: Two romances. Gotaso and Pumsuk: the wedding and wedding night [17]–[21] are brief and tender but generic. Gotaso loses the comic voice she had in #12, and “We will be happy forever!” [15] is a strong irony plant that pays off at #23 [48]–[49]. Sunduk and Yushin [26]–[57] is the best romance writing in the slice: twenty years of desire, an obstacle that is the crown itself, escalation in one step and one sentence (“Two horses. Tonight would be enough.”), a choice with a cost (“One more step and I do not stop.” / “…Then I will not take it.”), and a sting (“That is the sound you make when you have won.” / “…Then neither of us has.”). It is earned by #1 [55]–[60] and #11 [26], and it is played, not told.
episodes.best: “Don’t thank me. / That is the sound you make when you have won.” [52]
episodes.worst: [58]–[64]: two after-the-climax scenes that go back in time and introduce a merchant who doesn’t matter until #40.
fixes: Dramatize the father’s vow [1]–[7] as a two-hander between Chunchu and Pumsuk.
Cut [58]–[64] and end on [57], or on the Daeya cart [23]–[24] moved to the end.
Cut [10.0] and the cryptic aunt exchange [11]–[14], or card Chunmyung as Chunchu’s mother.

episodes.title: Munhee
episodes.verdict: A strong courtship that loses its shape at the pyre and overstays in bed: put Munhee in danger at the pyre, confess once, and cut ‘The Closed Months’ to a third.
episodes.romance: Desire is played on both sides: she buys the dream and steps forward to sew [13], and he keeps coming back ‘needing nothing sewn’ [18]. The escalation (needle, breath, her mouth above his pulse [19]) is the best slow burn in the slice. Munhee leads the dialogue with real wit (“Only the coat. / Or… your restraint as well.” [24]); Chunchu speaks in breathy fragments that sound like Pumsuk’s (“coming apart at the door” [25]). The obstacle (he won’t propose; the disgrace) and the costly choice (his public confession) are there but muddled at the pyre. Yushin’s “You did not choose my sister. I chose you.” [39] is a great turn. The payoff overstays: weeks of bedroom summary instead of one scene. We root for Munhee.
episodes.best: “Sister. Sell me that dream.” / “…For what?” / “My silk skirt.” [4]–[6]
episodes.worst: [50]–[67]: ‘The Closed Months’ restates one beat for eighteen blocks in summary and shot-list language.
fixes: Rebuild the pyre [33]–[47]: Munhee by the green wood, one confession, the Gaya talk moved after.
Cut ‘The Closed Months’ [50]–[67] to about six blocks of actual scene.
Fix the continuity at [48], [70] and [72].

episodes.title: Academy
episodes.verdict: Yeon’s voice is a joy but the scene has no stakes: merge it with #16 and #17 so the monk’s grudge and the uncle’s supper lead straight into Dosuryu’s warning.
episodes.best: “The Buddha’s fine. Fat, quiet, never asked me for anything. / It’s his landlords I mind.” [15]
episodes.worst: [21] and [27]: records that repeat or blunt the scene’s own lines.
fixes: Merge #15–#17 into one episode: academy gate, then the stone, then Dosuryu’s boots.
Cut the quotes at [10], [21] and [27].
Use one son’s trait in the scene, or cut the son cards to one line each.

episodes.title: Stele
episodes.verdict: A 241-word stop with three records and no scene: fold its one good question into #15 or #17.
episodes.best: “Aw… that’s it? A big rock?” [3]
episodes.worst: [6]–[8]: three quotes, two of them the same fact, filling most of the episode.
fixes: Fold [3]–[5] into the end of #15 or the start of #17 and retire #16 as an episode.
Cut the duplicate tribute quotes [7]/[8].
Give the stone scene one reaction from a son.

episodes.title: Dosuryu
episodes.verdict: The tightest scene in the slice; move the two ‘plan leaked’ records out of the middle so the laugh, the stop and the list run together.
episodes.best: “Then I’ll make a list too. / Mine’ll be longer.” [15]
episodes.worst: [11]–[12]: duplicate records interrupting the turn.
fixes: Absorb #16’s stone question as part of Yeon’s laugh (“Sixty-four fortresses, and they think a wall will hold me?”).
Fix the ‘late in the year’ to March slip at the seam into #18.

episodes.title: King Euija
episodes.verdict: Euija’s voice carries it: open on the dragon instead of the death notice, cut the maids’ chamber to a few lines, and point the ‘sentence that kills him’ tease at the right line.
episodes.romance: Not a romance. The maids’ banter characterizes Euija’s appetite (‘before the wine years’) and has wit, but it is three scenes with no arc and should be one.
episodes.best: “It was four lacquered paper kites, a low mist, six boatmen paid in advance…” [8]
episodes.worst: [50]–[62]: the maids’ chamber, an innuendo loop that stops the episode.
fixes: Open on the dragon [7]–[8]; cut the records [1]–[2].
Cut the chamber [50]–[62] to four lines and remove the nation’s line [63].
Move the tease [49] next to the line it means; unify Sungchung/Seongchung.

episodes.title: Yunchung
episodes.verdict: A sharp war council buried in an Assembly lecture: cut the shipping-writ false start and the third Rock explainer, fix ‘Goryeo’ and Yunchung’s ‘done for’, and let the narrator wink that Daeya is where Gotaso lives.
episodes.battle: War setup, not battle. The stakes are clear and personal: a king who needs a victory to own his own army [7]–[8]. The target gets a one-line map (“The last wall between Baekje and the Silla capital” [45]), and the general is believable. Missing: any plan or geography beyond ‘ten thousand men, by autumn’, and the dramatic irony that the reader knows who lives there.
episodes.best: “Tell me. Who rules Baekje?” / “Your Majesty does. / On paper.” [3]–[4]
episodes.worst: [11]–[20]: a false-start quarrel about berths, then the Rock explained for the third time.
fixes: Cut [12]–[15] and [18]–[20]; go from the private meeting to the chant [24] and the theme line [27].
Replace ‘Goryeo’ at [27]–[28] and fix Yunchung’s line at [46].
Add one narrator line at Daeya [45] tying it to Gotaso’s cart at #13 [23].

episodes.title: The Severing
episodes.verdict: A grim, effective legend once it reaches the night road: tell the betrayal once, drop the Nihon Shoki memorial, and use one name for the Cloud King.
episodes.battle: Not a battle: a summarized campaign, then one dramatized ambush and execution. The stakes (a king’s life, Baekje’s pride) are clear. The POV character, Seong, is carded at [6], so we care about him for about eighteen blocks. Geography is evocative but vague (“a ditch that was not there at dusk” [11]). The plan and reversal (Silla’s ambush) happen offstage. Cost and consequence are strong and concrete: the knife, the neck, the skull under the north hall steps. It works as legend, but it doesn’t show Baekje why it lost.
episodes.best: “He unfastens his own knife, gives it to the kneeling man, and puts his neck out.” [24]
episodes.worst: [1]–[8]: three tellings of the betrayal and a record full of names before the night road.
fixes: Cut [1]/[3]/[4] to one telling and drop the memorial [8].
Mask Muryuk’s speaker label on [16] and [22].
Call him the Cloud King at [12] and sharpen Dodo’s ‘oath’ irony at [21].

episodes.title: Gumil
episodes.verdict: Length not earned: cut the cavern opening [0]–[92] (#45 Seohyun retells its origin story anyway), open at Daeya as #20’s card promised, and spend the space giving Gumil a voice and a grievance on the page.
episodes.romance: Three strands. (1) The cavern scenes are erotic comedy, not romance: there’s no obstacle except Yushin saying “Her Majesty”, and the goddesses narrate their own poses and wants, which is caption-dialogue ([10.38] “I’ll keep my knees together. That’s a lie.”, [28]). Yushin does sleep with Narim [44]–[62] a year after #13, where he refused the queen (“Then I will not take it”), and nothing reflects on it, so it cheapens his best romance. (2) Gumil and Maehwa are the real romance, and they’re good in the little room they get: poverty is the obstacle, and the banter has subtext ([106]–[107] “Buy me clothes, then. / Everything I own refuses to fit.” / “…You know what I am paid.”), plus warmth before the fall [125]. That’s about 200 words of their talk against about 4,000 for the cavern. (3) Pumsuk’s desire at the feast [130]–[137] is all told: heart-pupils, drool, then a monologue saying what he wants.
episodes.best: Maehwa, the night before: “Keep your hand on my waist. / It does not have to be a True Bone hand.” [125]
episodes.worst: [0]–[92]: about 4,000 words of repetitive cavern erotica about three characters who aren’t in this story, sitting where the promised Gumil episode should start.
fixes: Cut [0]–[92] from this episode and open at [93]. #45 Seohyun tells the First Kim visit properly, and #23 [67]–[84] already has a cavern scene if one is wanted after Daeya.

Make Gumil the protagonist the title promises: a scene before Pumsuk arrives (signing tallies under a purple sleeve, bowing to a 24-year-old at the gate), his [98]–[100] grievance said to someone, and the marriage beats [104]–[108] and [124]–[128] expanded into the episode’s heart.
Merge the two yard scenes ([109]–[116], [117]–[122]) into one, strip the image-prompt narration, and end the feast on Maehwa’s line [136] and Pumsuk’s exit [138].

episodes.title: Maehwa
episodes.verdict: Length not earned: the story moves one step (the affair happens; Gotaso’s name turns it), so cut to about 800 words. Explicitness isn’t the problem, repetition is. Decide what the night means and let the record’s “took her” bite.
episodes.romance: The slice’s central romance is played almost entirely as sex. Desire is vivid and the opening has real chemistry ([15] “You were counting. Not the cup. / My mouth. Seventeen.”; her fake exit [24]–[25]), and the obstacles are big: his wife is Chunchu’s daughter, her husband is his officer. But the escalation is by position, not emotion. “I love you” arrives mid-act ([74], [77]–[78]), the narrator asserts love ([75], [79]), and his silent exit [81] contradicts it. No choice costs him anything on the page; others pay in #23. A reader who rooted for Pumsuk and Gotaso in #12–#13 gets no beat of his conflict over her, so the turn reads as whiplash, not tragedy.
episodes.best: “You were counting. Not the cup. / My mouth. Seventeen.” [15]: a poor woman counting a noble’s glances out loud.
episodes.worst: [30]–[80]: about 2,100 words of a single escalating sex scene that repeats one beat in porn-parody register and moves the plot once.
fixes: Cut [30]–[80] to one paragraph around the Gotaso-name turn [49]–[52]; keep a trimmed [0]–[27] for the seduction and its banter.
Give Pumsuk one beat with Gotaso’s ribbon [5] that he consciously walks past, so his line to Kangrim in #23 [41] (“I wanted the love and the oath to be one thing”) has a plant.
Decide whether the night is seduction, coercion or love, and use the record [82] as a sting instead of a footnote.

episodes.title: Siege of Daeya
episodes.verdict: The grief in Surabol is the best writing in the slice, but the siege never happens on the page: stage the fall from one POV, fix the order of the deaths, and cut the opening sex and the cavern coda.
episodes.romance: Two marriages end, and both endings work. Gumil and Maehwa’s last exchange [13]–[17] (“You are trash as well.” / “That is the last thing they ever say to each other.”) is cruel and true. Gotaso’s death [27]–[38] pays off #12–#13: asked whether she chose the man or the vow, she says “Both. / Is that allowed?” and remembers her father’s stained coat (#12 [18]–[19]). Both are undercut by placement: comic sex before the first [5]–[10], cavern flirting after the second [67]–[84].
episodes.battle: The stakes are clear and personal: Daeya is the last wall before the Silla capital (#19 [45]), and Chunchu’s daughter is inside. But the siege isn’t dramatized. There’s no POV on the walls, no geography (where is the granary gate relative to the inner room?), no defenders’ plan, and no staged reversal; the betrayal happens in three sentences [19]–[21]. The famous last stand (Jukjuk) exists only as records [50], [53]. The surrender and massacre [43]–[45] are two lines of dialogue and one of narration. Cost and consequence land in Surabol instead ([52]–[61] are excellent). Verdict: summarized as ‘the gate opens, they die’.
episodes.best: Chunchu on his mother’s knee: “you count the territory it cost. / This one… I can’t find the edge of it.” [59]
episodes.worst: [18]–[45]: the fall of Daeya is about 130 words of summary, with two people opening the gate and the deaths in the wrong order.
fixes: Dramatize the fall from Gumil’s POV on the granary wall (expand [19]–[23] into a scene), with Jukjuk’s refusal as dialogue in place of the [50] record.
Reorder [27]–[47]: surrender oath → broken → Gotaso → Kangrim → Pumsuk → news in Surabol. Delete [42] and [25].
Cut the opening sex [5]–[10] and the cavern coda [67]–[84]; end on Bupmin and Munhee [66].

episodes.title: Yeon’s Massacre
episodes.verdict: A strong ritual set-piece that pays off #8 precisely. Cut three of the five records and the cards-and-diagram pile after it so the killing and its aftermath keep their momentum.
episodes.battle: A massacre rather than a battle, and the best-staged violence in the slice. It has stakes (Yeon is on a death list, #17 [5]), a trap (the doors close from outside [10]) and a ritual structure: five commanders, each killed on a callback to what he said at #8’s Summit ([14], [18], [22], [30]), each sword added to Yeon’s back. Then the king [32]–[34], with “May You live ten thousand years” turned into the killing line. Weaknesses: [11] summarizes the slaughter before the ritual begins, and records retell it afterwards.
episodes.best: “Uncle. / You told me to sit down. / …. / A Yeon takes this one from a Yeon.” [30]
episodes.worst: [36]–[55]: five records, cards and a diagram after the massacre, three of the records retelling what was just shown.
fixes: Cut records [37], [51] and [55] and the diagram [45]; move the Bojang name beat [52]–[54] to follow [42].
Replace [11]’s summary with one image, and name the emperor at [34].
Give the ‘traitor’ callback to Gusesa (#8 [25]), or plant Lee Gaesa earlier.

episodes.title: Chunchu & Yeon
episodes.verdict: A real thriller with a clock, a mystery and wit. Untangle the release order so the rabbit letter and Yushin’s army both cause it.
episodes.best: Chunchu to Yeon: “Pride is a decoration for men who can afford to lose.” [26], then the guards’ bet and the bloody hand [31]–[37].
episodes.worst: [57]–[74]: the release is scrambled, and the letter Chunchu risked writing doesn’t matter.
fixes: Reorder the release so the rabbit letter and Yushin’s army both cause it; cut the split-screen gag [59]–[63].
Cut the re-announcement [1]–[5].
Gloss Hangyul at [7]; change “Boy” to “Old man” at [74].

episodes.title: Euija & Yeon
episodes.verdict: Euija at his wittiest and a satisfying payoff of the hand. Give it a real opening, and cut the two plan-restating records and the maids coda.
episodes.romance: Not romance: [53]–[62] is a short sexual aside with two maids that adds nothing.
episodes.best: Euija: “only one has actually murdered a king of Goryeo. It was not me.” [17]
episodes.worst: [53]–[62]: the maids coda, plus the restating records [38]–[39].
fixes: Replace [0]–[2] with a hook line in Euija’s voice.
Cut the maids scene [53]–[62] and end on [63].

episodes.title: Nangbi
episodes.verdict: The slice’s best episode: a clean standalone that earns Yushin’s legend through his enemies. Cut the record that retells the charge, and give the charge one beat from the trench.
episodes.battle: One charge, summarized [7] and retold by a record [8]. It still works, because the stakes are personal (a son asking his father, helmet off, in front of an army [4]–[5]) and the payoff is understated: “…Your helmet’s crooked.” [10]–[11]. The heroics are reported through the enemy ([14], [18], [23]–[31]), exactly the house standard for reputations. There’s no geography or plan, but none is needed at this length.
episodes.best: Seohyun, with a general’s head at his feet: “…Your helmet’s crooked.” [10], then he straightens it with both hands [11].
episodes.worst: [7]–[8]: the charge happens in summary, and then a record says it again.
fixes: Cut [8]; put one sensory beat of the charge into [7].
Fix the #26 card to name the sword, not “one Silla name”.
Clarify Taejo’s Colossal River role against #8 [15].

episodes.title: Forty Fortresses
episodes.verdict: A summary that contradicts its neighbours: decide who is taking forty fortresses (the record in #26 says Euija; #31 says Silla is losing them), then dramatize one campaign beat instead of quoting it.
episodes.romance: The cavern scene [14]–[25] is the same flirtation for the fourth time; not romance.
episodes.battle: None dramatized: forty fortresses in one sentence [5], one record [6], one map [7].
episodes.best: Yushin: “If I stopped, they would invent a reason for my stopping.” [12]
episodes.worst: [14]–[25]: a repeat cavern visit with stale counsel.
fixes: Resolve the forty-fortress contradiction with #26 [39] and #31 [43].
Dramatize the gate-and-water anecdote [13]; cut the cavern [14]–[25].
Replace the opener [0] with a hook (start on Euija’s breakfast panic [2]).

episodes.title: The Eastern Star
episodes.verdict: A good triptych that pays off #1’s star. Anchor the cold open in a place, and plant or cut Gyebek’s “I saw Gesomun again”.
episodes.best: “…I told you. That one is a planet.” / “Thirty years and you are still saying that.” [6]–[7]
episodes.worst: [14]–[15]: an unplanted line that opens a mystery the book never answers.
fixes: Plant or cut Gyebek’s Gesomun sighting and scar [14]–[15].
Give [0] a place and time.
Name whom Yeon addresses at the cave [22].

episodes.title: Emperor
episodes.verdict: A 199-word stub that #31 replays: fold it into #31 as its cold open, or give the emperor one short scene in place of two records.
episodes.best: “He turns it over on his tongue, like a grape he hasn’t decided to eat.” [0]
episodes.worst: [2]–[4]: two records and a card where a scene should be.
fixes: Merge into #31’s opening, or give the emperor a three-line exchange that delivers [3]’s content as dialogue.

episodes.title: Four Dragons
episodes.verdict: A setup anthology with no one to follow: open on the name taboo, keep the dying minister and the farmer's wife, and cut the news roundup, the Korean-only dragon table and the Longmen record pile.
episodes.romance: Xue Rengui and Lady Liu [57]–[65] is a marriage, not a romance, but it is the episode's warmest beat: she pushes him out the door ('You're not a hoe. You're a ji.') and he asks the ancestors to wait. It is undercut when the narrator and a quote retell her line ([62]–[63]) and an opera aside follows ([69]–[70]); Liu and the unburied ancestors never come back.
episodes.best: The mirror speech: 'With a man for a mirror, he sees his own faults. …Today I lose one of my mirrors.' [14]
episodes.worst: [54]–[70]: the Longmen field buries a nice marriage scene under an edict, three quotes and two asides about later opera and Lü Bu.
fixes: Open on the name taboo [3]–[8] (fix the speaker at [7]) and cut the bio [0]–[2]. It hooks, and it plants the slice's best motif: the emperor nobody may name against the Guardian nobody wrote down.
Cut the rant and the news roundup ([15]–[17], [20]–[21]) and the Longmen record pile ([62]–[63], [67]–[70]); cut [71], which spends #34.
Either make the four dragons people (one English line each, with a want) or retitle the episode and drop the table [31].

episodes.title: Yodong
episodes.verdict: A strong hook and one great human beat (the shrine bride), but the fall of Yodong and 'the rest of the line' are summary: let the bride carry the fall and cut the table.
episodes.battle: Stakes are told by the narrator rather than felt. The wall [0], the road torn up behind the army [5] ('Nobody goes home the way they came') and the emperor throwing earth into the moat [6] are good commander beats. But nobody inside Yodong has a face except the bride (two lines); the fall [14] is a paragraph of catapults, towers and a south wind; and 'the rest of the line' [23]–[25] is a list. No defender POV, no plan, no reversal: X falls, Y falls.
episodes.best: 'It's… heavy. The dress. / …Tell my mum. Tell her I didn't cry.' [10]
episodes.worst: [22]–[25]: a summary paragraph, a map and an eight-row table stand in for a month of war.
fixes: Let the shrine bride carry the fall: cut the quote [13] and add one beat in [14] where the fire or the Tang reach the shrine door.
Replace [23]–[25] with one dramatized fort (the White Dragon's spear, the lord who opens the gate anyway) and cut the table.
Rewrite the Ansi exchange [19]–[21] as a duel of wit about names, then end the episode on the relief army choosing the open field, so #33's lesson has a target.

episodes.title: Boiling River
episodes.verdict: A 390-word note, half of it records, whose one lesson ('I did not look at the ground') never fires in the battle it foreshadows: fold it into #34, or make the officer who dies in the king's robes the story.
episodes.battle: Summarized: two wins in a clause, the loss in a sentence [4], Hwando burning in a sentence [6], then two quotes. The single dramatic image, a king admitting 'I did not look at the ground' [5], works. The officer in the royal robes is a battle-ending sacrifice told in half a line.
episodes.best: '…I did not look at the ground.' [5]
episodes.worst: [8]–[9]: two record quotes that repeat what [3]–[4] just said.
fixes: Fold this into #34 as three or four blocks: an old Goguryeo officer tells Go Yeonsu the Boiling River story before Stallion Mountain, and Go Yeonsu ignores him.
If it stays an episode, dramatize the officer in the king's robes [6] (who he is, why he volunteers, the walk out) and cut the quotes [8]–[9].
Fix the Dongchun/Dongcheon spelling ([0], [1], [5]) and name the empire so the reader doesn't think it's Tang.

episodes.title: Stallion Mountain
episodes.verdict: Three good human stories (Sul Gedu, Xue, the Yeon boys) wrapped around a battle that is three sentences and two identical quotes: dramatize the battle from Goguryeo's side and cut the duplicate record.
episodes.battle: This is the invasion's big field battle, and it is summarized. Goguryeo's stakes (its only field army; if it loses, Ansi stands alone) are never said. The POV is entirely Tang: the emperor, Xue, Sul Gedu. There is no geography beyond 'the crow road' and a mountain, no plan and no reversal, and the thunderstorm survives only in the quotes. In the real battle the emperor signalled from the mountain with drums while his generals closed from behind: the four dragons' moment, in an arc that named an episode after them. Cost is told in a clause (thirty-six thousand surrender, three thousand Mohe buried alive [23]). Sul Gedu is the best device, a Silla man fighting 'Samhan men' for a sash and found deepest in the line, but we never see him fight or choose.
episodes.best: 'You took it for me.' / 'I am the elder.' [53]–[54]
episodes.worst: [12]–[16]: the battle is three sentences and two duplicate quotes.
fixes: Dramatize Stallion Mountain from Goguryeo's side: Go Yeonsu chooses the open field over an old officer's Boiling River warning (paying off #33), the emperor's drums on the mountain, the dragons closing behind, Xue's charge as the turn. Cut quote [16].
Play Sul Gedu's death and the imperial robe [26]–[27] as a scene and keep [28]; trim or cut the cell break-out [29]–[42].
Replace [0] with a real hook, e.g. Sul Gedu's 'In Silla they count your bones before they hire you.'

episodes.title: Colossal River
episodes.verdict: One of the great trickster stories delivered as an edict, two maps, a formation card, a poem widget and two quotes, with no dialogue at all: dramatize the seven surrenders and the poem, or fold it into Ansi.
episodes.battle: Not dramatized. The seven fake surrenders, the poem, the half-crossed river and the strike on the rearguard exist only as summary [5], a widget [8] and a quote [10]. No POV, no scene, no voice.
episodes.best: The poem's last line: 'know it is enough, and I pray you stop.' [8], the only moment with a personality in it.
episodes.worst: [1]–[11]: the whole episode is records and widgets.
fixes: Dramatize it: Munduk walking into the Sui camp, the seven surrenders, the general reading the poem, the river half-crossed. That is a Prince Euija-shaped story (a want, an obstacle, a trick, a payoff).
Or cut it as an episode and fold three blocks into #36 as an Ansi soldier's memory.
Open on a hook instead of '…in the year 612' [0]; cut the edict [1] and one of the two closing quotes [10]/[11].

episodes.title: Ansi
episodes.verdict: The earthen-mountain sequence is the best battle writing in the slice, but the climax evaporates into a shot-list fragment, weather and three quotes: stage the emperor's wounding, the retreat through the marsh, and the farewell bow.
episodes.battle: The only fully dramatized battle beat in the slice. The race between shovels [10]–[16] and the collapse-and-seize reversal [17]–[23] have geography (mound, wall, gap), a plan, a reversal and a cost (Fu Fuai beheaded [24]). The Guardian is a good POV but a thin one, with seven lines here. Then the climax deflates: the emperor's wounding [26] is hedged ('Whether it was the wall or a stone') and written like an image prompt, the retreat [28]–[29] is weather, and 'for the first time in his life, the Second Emperor knew defeat' is told. The Guardian never makes a choice that costs him, and the two men never face each other again, though the slice spent six episodes setting up the man nobody may name against the man nobody wrote down.
episodes.best: 'Never mind the wall. Who's up on that thing right now?' [19]
episodes.worst: [25]–[37]: the climax is a shot-list fragment, a weather report, a map and three record quotes.
fixes: Stage the climax: the emperor rides too close, an arrow comes from the wall (the Guardian's), and the exposed face [26] becomes a moment between the two men instead of a camera note. Cut the spoilers [4]–[5] and the decoder [8].
Make the retreat a scene in the marsh he tore up (#32 [5]) and put 'Had he been alive, he would not have let me make this expedition' [31] in his mouth there.
End on one staged farewell: the Guardian bows from the wall, the silk goes up, the emperor asks for a name and gets none. Cut [33], [36], [37]; move or cut [38].

episodes.title: Haemosu
episodes.verdict: A genuinely fun, sexy myth built on a real game (her name for his descent), but Haemosu's side of the cost is missing: show why he leaves, and cut the three quotes that retell and contradict the scene.
episodes.romance: The best-built seduction in the slice. Desire is instant ('Stop. Stop the chariot.' [12]). The obstacle is a rule (the sun's hour, the sisters diving, the father). Escalation runs on a real game: he wants her name before he comes down, she makes him come down first ('From the sky it's an order. At the water… I'll hear it as a request.' [24]), and she gives it only at the climax [48]–[49]. The banter has chemistry ('Then I should blink.' / 'I'm not a lamp.' [30]–[31]). She chooses, staying when her sisters dive [19], and she pays: banishment [55]–[62], with Habek's 'Say a name' turning the motif against her. What's missing is his choice and his cost. We never see him leave or learn why, so the romance's second act (his absence) reads as a contradiction rather than an obstacle. The payoff arrives two episodes later in #39 [255].
episodes.best: 'Come down first. / From the sky it's an order. / At the water… I'll hear it as a request.' [24]
episodes.worst: [71]–[76]: a quote retells the episode in Yuhwa's mouth, then two identical quotes give a different conception.
fixes: Add one beat after [51] showing why Haemosu leaves (the hour, heaven calling, a punishment) so his absence is an obstacle, not a contradiction.
Cut the quotes [71] and [76] (and probably [75]); let the sun-shaft [72] do the work.
Open on the logline's two sentences and fold [0]'s chariot description in after.

episodes.title: Buyeo
episodes.verdict: Propulsive and funny, with a clean chain of cause and effect: cut the three turtle quotes at the climax and the stable quote that spoils the stable scene, and plant the half-sword Lady Ye will need in #67.
episodes.romance: Jumong and Lady Ye get a widget [28], one sentence [29] and two lines [49]–[50]: 'a hall's solution'. The farewell ('Leave the door half open. So I know which way is still yours.') is lovely, and it plants an obstacle that #39's romance ignores.
episodes.battle: Not a battle but a chase: Daeso's riders 'less a hunt than a net' [52], a split at the ridge [55]–[59], a fall, a reaper [63]–[65], a rescue. The geography is clear (pines, ridge, river) and the stakes are personal. The rescue is a god from the machine, but it plays as comedy between two brothers, and Jumong does the decisive thing himself by shouting his lineage [74].
episodes.best: 'You just robbed a ledger.' / 'I borrowed a day. / I'll give it back.' [83]–[84]
episodes.worst: [76]–[78]: three record quotes of the same turtle bridge interrupt the escape at its peak.
fixes: Cut the turtle quotes [76]–[78] (or keep one) and move the stable quote [34] after the stable scene.
Plant the half-sword in Lady Ye's farewell [49]–[50] so #67's payoff has a setup, and give the knife attempt [47] two real beats.
Introduce Oi, Mari and Hyupbo before the flight [52] and cut Galsa-Buyeo [26].

episodes.title: Jolbon
episodes.verdict: The best romance-comedy scenes in the slice live here, but at 5,200 words it's twice its story: cut the repeated tsundere beats and the extra bedroom sequences, dramatize the founding, use Jumong's wife as the obstacle, and end on Yuhwa's ascension instead of five codas.
episodes.romance: The slice's best romance and the nearest thing in it to the Prince Euija standard. Desire runs both ways from the first hall scene ('Pretty. Just—' / 'Eyes. Front.' / 'Count the dirt. Not him.' [24]–[27]). The obstacles are status (he is her slave [35]), her pride and her father. Escalation is real: the nickname, jealousy at the well ([110]–[126]; 'They can do sexy. She can do eldest' [112]), her name given at the well [131] (a clean echo of Yuhwa's name game), the kiss, the stolen keepsakes [144], his walk-away [150], her arrow past his ear [152], the confession into the dirt [160]. That confession is earned and funny, and the hundred paces [193]–[203] gives her father a great reluctant blessing. Problems: the first kiss is narrated in one sentence [136] while lesser beats get full scenes; the walk-away is unmotivated; Jumong's wife and unborn son (#38) are never mentioned, so 'Only you. From the first look.' [167] reads as a lie the book doesn't know it's telling; the escalation loops in [57]–[82]; and the bedroom sequences ([87], [89]–[91], [171]–[182], [224]–[227]) repeat one joke four times. The grain room does pay off structurally (her hidden voice exposed and accepted), so trim it rather than cut it. Haemosu and Yuhwa's payoff from #37 also lands here: 'You're late. / The copper room… stayed warm.' [255.3] is the most moving line in the slice, buried in a coda.
episodes.best: The arrow past his ear and the confession: 'I wasn't going to say it. / I was gonna let you leave. Stupid. Fine.' [152]–[160]
episodes.worst: [228]–[257]: an errand to a new kingdom, a generic blessing ('Build a world of your own'), a cameo by the sons, a spoiler line, a mislabelled flashback, a death in a subordinate clause and a cryptic coda.
fixes: Cut about 2,000 words: [58]–[62] and [66]–[76] (the loop), [85]–[88] (one loft scene is enough), half of [172]–[182], [224]–[227], and [228]–[238] unless the horse pays off there.
Use Lady Ye: let Sosuno learn that Jumong left a pregnant wife in Buyeo, and make that the fight that ends with his bow on the ground [150]. It motivates the walk-away and plants #67.

Dramatize the founding (one ditch, two cousins, Jumong with an unstrung bow [210]) and end on Yuhwa's ascension [255] as a clean coda. Cut [254] and the 'year Yuri comes south' clause in [256], which spoil #67, and either explain or cut 'Go exile' [257].

episodes.title: Gi (起)
episodes.verdict: A strong inciting episode buried under a cold open in Yamato: start on the council veto and Bidam owns the episode from its first line.
episodes.romance: Only Munhee packing for Chunchu [2]–[5]: 'Then I will pack for more.' Married shorthand in three lines, played, not told. Nothing else.
episodes.best: [89] “So, for the first time in his life, Bidam decides something without a vote.” Close second: [74] “Chunchu is across the sea. His orders, apparently, are not.”
episodes.worst: [0]–[18], the Yamato cold open: two unknown names, two records and a merchant's tips out of order. None of it is Bidam's, and it stands between the reader and the episode's spine.
fixes: Open on the veto ([29]–[41]) with a one-line hook (“In a council that needs every hand, one stays down.”). Fold the voyage into Bidam's discovery at [60] in three blocks.
Rewrite the Seungman gate scene [45]–[48]: give Bidam his own reply, not Chunchu's Gesomun line from [12].
Cut the council explainer [24]–[26] and the table [28]; keep the veto diagram [32].

episodes.title: Suro
episodes.verdict: A pleasant erotic fairy tale in the wrong place: it stops the rebellion one block after Bidam decides to rebel and gives the reader nothing the siege needs. Move it out of the arc or cut it to a 400-word ink interlude.
episodes.romance: Two romances, both desire with no obstacle. Ibiga and the Lady [5]–[15] is pure appetite; there is nothing to root for. Suro and Heo has real chemistry because she leads and he can't speak: 'Once? What a modest king.' [65] / 'I am not modest. …I am only holding on.' [66]. But the only obstacle, language, is played for heat, not cost, and nobody chooses anything that costs them. The best beat, 'My country is gone. Only the name is left.' [70], arrives after the sex as an afterthought. Played rather than told, but repetitive.
episodes.best: [71] “Then we keep the name. I can always make another country.” Also the narrator at [25]: “At some point one has to ask what the birds were doing.”
episodes.worst: [51]–[61]: the second and third sex passages repeat the first, with no new information and no turn, while the rebellion waits.
fixes: Take it out of the rebellion: place it before #40 or after #47 (or merge it with #43), so #40 [89] cuts straight to Day 1.
Cut it by half: two blocks for Ibiga ([6], [13]); keep the court meeting [37]–[44] and the morning [62]–[67]; one ¶ for the tent.
Merge the two births ([16], [22]) and make the last beat point at Yushin, so the episode earns a slot in his story.

episodes.title: Seung (承)
episodes.verdict: The arc's engine works (a ten-day clock and a nightly tea duel that escalates); open on the sickbed instead of a record, and halve the Day 4 debate so the rant hits harder.
episodes.romance: The Dukman triangle is told, not played: [32] 'same impossible orbit around Princess Dukman. They do not say the word love.' A good line, and Bidam's threat at [32.6] is charming, but it is the only Bidam–Dukman beat in the whole arc. Bupmin's cavern cameo [47]–[51] is light flirtation ('you are shaped like a problem I want in my lap'), harmless and funny.
episodes.battle: No battle on the page: the siege is 'Arrows trade; messengers lie' [34]. The real combat is the tea duel, and as a duel it works: stakes (the grain clock), two people we care about, escalation (blood [27]–[29], then colonisation [36], policy [56]–[67], 'never of Silla' [89]), and a plan with a reversal (keep him talking, splash him, nothing rises). The Jade Gate flashback [40] is summary.
episodes.best: [77] “Have you ever… even for a SECOND… considered the POSSIBILITY… that your ideas are simply terrible?” The palace's psychological gambit backfires; it is the arc's best turn.
episodes.worst: [62]–[67]: six alternating position papers on Day 4. They carry the arc's thesis, but nobody interrupts and nobody wins a point.
fixes: Open on [2] and the sickbed [4]–[9]; cut the opening record [0].
Halve the Day 4 debate [62]–[67] and let Bupmin's jar interrupt it.
Plant the conscience water before this episode, cut the Sadaham aside [32.4]–[32.5], and fix 'cousins' [4] and 'elder brother' [97.4].

episodes.title: Muryuk
episodes.verdict: Too thin to pay off the mystery box: cut the Sadaham opener and open on #20's night road, so the reader learns who the cone-helm man was.
episodes.battle: Sadaham's 'They said too young. The gate didn't.' [3] stands in for a battle. The real fight is the surrender [13]–[18], a negotiation with one move each, and it is the best part.
episodes.best: [17] “Three generations later, his grandson will still be told he is not really one of them.”
episodes.worst: [0]–[8]: a recap of Sadaham's episode and a record about a different Gaya, before the prince appears.
fixes: Open on the #20 night road: the cone helm in the ditch, King Seong on the camp stool, then the name Muryuk. In #20, give those two lines an anonymous speaker so the name holds until here.
Cut [2]–[8] and one of the two records.
Give Muryuk one more bargaining line [13]–[16] so the deal visibly costs him something.

episodes.title: Jeon (轉)
episodes.verdict: The reversal episode delivers (the kite and the horse sacrifice are the arc's best sequence), but Day 7's two long cavern scenes and the ghost speeches stall it, and Day 9's battle is one sentence.
episodes.romance: Yushin in the cavern [31]–[42] is Golhwa's want against his queen ('She is not in the water, Yushin. We are.' [38]). Narim's 'he took the armour off and still kept her name on' [41] is the arc's best line about Yushin and Sunduk. The Cheongwan flashback [62] is a dark mini-romance told in three sentences (he beheads the horse that carried him to her door). Bidam's cavern scene [15]–[29] is humiliation, not romance.
episodes.battle: The psychological battle is the best in the arc: a plan (the star omen, 'Heaven has already voted' [52]), a reversal (the burning kite [56]), a cost (Hangyul, [64]–[71]) and a consequence on the other side (Bidam puts his beads away [73]). The physical battle is missing: 'Assault and counter-assault' [80] is the only fighting in ten days, with no geography, no point of view, and the co-leader's death in a clause.
episodes.best: [68] Yushin to Hangyul: “…I'm sorry. This time I'm the one who brought you.” With [61], the groom who “starts to cry with his mouth shut.”
episodes.worst: [15]–[48], Day 7: an explicit humiliation, then a flirt, then ghosts, freezing the countdown between the Day 6 insult and the Day 8 omen.
fixes: Cut Day 7 by two-thirds: Bidam's expulsion ending on 'The lake keeps Kims. It does not keep slogans.', the ghosts at one line each.
Dramatize Day 9 [80]: one assault, and Yumjong dying on the page.
Resolve the headband so #40 [67], [4] here and #46 [58] agree.

episodes.title: Seohyun
episodes.verdict: The best romance in the slice and the most Prince Euija-shaped episode, wedged into the worst slot (between Day 9 and Day 10, after his own ghost has spoken) and bloated by a rerun of #21 and a pile of records. Move it before #44 and cut it by a third.
episodes.romance: The real thing. Desire ('He looks. The histories… record exactly how.' [4]); an obstacle with teeth (a royal father, the Gaya stigma, a lock); escalation (lost horse, side gate, mulberry shed, proposal); chemistry in the talk ('Is the road that bad, or are you lost?' / 'It's lost. I'm only on it.' [11]–[12]; 'Not much me.' / '…I was going to say not much rice.' / 'Liar.' [26]–[28]); a costly choice (she crawls through a drain in her good silk [60]); and a payoff that calls back the first joke [65]–[68]. Played, not told. The clerk's wife is a gift.
episodes.best: [65]–[68] “Is the horse lost tonight?” / “…No. Tonight it knows exactly where it's going.”
episodes.worst: [111]–[148]: a near-verbatim replay of #21's cavern flashback, down to the oracle's words and the warm stone.
fixes: Move it out of the Day 9 to Day 10 gap: run it after #43, so #44 and #46 play straight through and the #44 ghosts are people we've met.
Cut the spring rerun [111]–[148] to a two-line callback; keep 'Your hair's wet. It hasn't rained in a week.' [153].
Cut the six records that retell the scene: [63], [81], [100], [102], [157], [170].

episodes.title: Gyeol (結)
episodes.verdict: The emotional payoffs are the best in the slice (109, Bisamun going north, 'Dukman', the untouched cup), but the duel is two sentences and Bidam's death is told three times out of order. Stage the fight and fix the sequence.
episodes.romance: The arc's best payoff. Forty-five episodes after #1, where she calls him 'Yushin-ah' for the last time, the dying queen asks him to say her name: 'Say the name I had before the room.' / 'Dukman.' / 'Yushin.' / 'I am here.' [49]–[52]. Subtext carries it ('I lost one. Which one, I will not say.' [45]). Played, restrained, earned. Its weakness is upstream: the 'queen between them' is all Yushin's; Bidam's love for her is told once (#42 [32]) and never played.
episodes.battle: The duel [8]–[9] is summary: no plan, no reversal, no geography, no beat-by-beat. What hurts is the aftermath, not the fight: 'One hundred and nine. Finally.' [10], Bisamun standing over him and walking north [16]–[18], the purge in Bidam's own words [19]–[24]. Cost and consequence are excellent; the fight itself is missing.
episodes.best: [49]–[52] “Say the name I had before the room.” / “Dukman.” / “Yushin.” / “I am here.”
episodes.worst: [8]–[29]: a two-sentence duel, then a death told three times in the wrong order, then a record that contradicts it.
fixes: Stage the duel ([8]–[9]) as a scene with a reversal that uses the yard and the score.
Reorder the death: Kangrim's exchange before the fall; cut the second fall [29] and the contradicting record [25].
Replace 'the opposite kite' with the father's binary ('A righteous traitor, or an unrighteous king?') and fix the 'twist' label [57].

episodes.title: Queen Jinduk
episodes.verdict: A clean, witty bridge with one dead stretch: cut one of the two identical investiture records and turn the fragmentary private audience into a short scene.
episodes.best: [1] “The succession Bidam died objecting to passes at last. Unanimously.” Also [15]–[16]: “…You had that ready.” / “Since the funeral, Majesty.”
episodes.worst: [2]–[3]: two investiture records in a row saying the same thing.
fixes: Cut one of the two investiture records [2]/[3].
Make [9]–[12] one real exchange about Bidam's 'never of Silla'.
Settle 'cousin' or 'sister' across #1, #40, #42 and #47.

episodes.title: Huangdi
episodes.verdict: The best material in the slice is here, buried in a 7,900-word tour: cut the two history flashbacks, the duplicate Wu scene and most widgets (about 1,500 words), hold the emperor’s yes until the Six Steeds so the army is the question, or split the episode at [177].
episodes.romance: No romance. Wu’s encounters are flirtation as threat (‘a little too close’ [197], the whisper [226], ‘paralyzed in fear’ [228]) and work as menace; the hallway turn, ‘How is she doing?’ [222], is the best Wu beat. The Li Zhi friendship [115]–[127], [246]–[251] has real chemistry (‘Brothers, then — of the inconvenient kind’ [126]) but no friction, so it charms rather than grips.
episodes.battle: No battle on stage. The Six Steeds [135]–[147], [159] are five told battle memories, vivid and wounded but monologue summary in identical shape. The Goguryeo patrol [256]–[263] is the only action and is over in four blocks.
episodes.best: ‘…Saluzi. / Your most loyal warrior. The one who never held office. / Majesty. He is a horse.’ [154], after 100 blocks of setup and a clerk’s wasted afternoon, capped by ‘You supplied that yourself’ [155].
episodes.worst: [210]–[211], the Gija & Wiman flashback: 300 words, five new names and a herald chorus, no link to Chunchu, and it opens the Joseon box 40 episodes early. Close behind: the First Emperor flashback [82].
fixes: Cut about 1,500 words that don’t serve the ask: [79]–[87] with the First Emperor flashback [82], the Gija & Wiman flashback [210]–[211], Wu’s banquet dialogue [195]–[204], [62] and [64]–[65], [89]–[92], two of the six horses, the three later diagrams, four idiom cards and the retelling quotes [177], [264]. If the author wants to keep the Tang texture, split at [177] instead: ‘Huangdi’ ends on ‘Baekje will be the single failure of yours’; a second episode runs banquet, hallway, the name, the gate and the sea.

Make the army the spine: cut the [36] quote and keep the emperor’s answer back (he wants Chunchu in his guard [50], keeps Inmun [60]) until the Six Steeds, so the dying man’s promise [169]–[171] is the turn. Replace the stage direction [167] with something shown.

Land On Gunhae: plant him in the ward count [15], give Chunchu one reaction in the small boat that echoes Saluzi (‘the only one who never once asked me for anything’ [161]), and end on the count (eleven came in; fewer go home) instead of the [264] quote.

episodes.title: Royal Secretariat
episodes.verdict: Swap it with #50, put the Harmony Council in the room to lose, and stage the Baekje edict as a scene instead of ending on 300 words of record.
episodes.best: ‘The crowns stay. Have you looked at them? Gold trees. Antlers. Little jade commas that ring when you nod.’ [38]
episodes.worst: [40]–[52]: four records in a row, ending the episode on a 300-word edict with no one on stage.
fixes: Swap #49 and #50 in reading order so the old emperor dies and Chunchu says ‘Then it is mine’ (#50 [25]) before he builds the Secretariat; move this ‘brush’ idea into #50’s card and give #48 a card that teases the emperor’s health.

Put the council on stage once: a councillor arrives with the border petition ready to debate it, and Jukji hands it back already sealed (this dramatizes [19]). Cut the opening diagrams [1]–[2] and [14].
Turn the edict [52] into a short Sabi scene: Euija reads ‘he may settle it with you in battle’ aloud with Gyebek in the room. It gives Baekje’s leads, offstage since #29, a beat before #56.

episodes.title: Jiabeng
episodes.verdict: A strong short montage hurt by an offstage death and three quotes that repeat what we just saw; give the emperor one line before he goes, and play this episode before #49.
episodes.romance: Li Zhi and Wu at Ganye [31]–[34]: two lines carry desire and taboo (she was his father’s woman, set up at [27]–[29]). ‘Lady Wu. …They cut your hair.’ / ‘Hair grows back, Majesty.’ is played, not told. Short and good.
episodes.best: ‘He made me promise to finish it. And then he left orders to stop. …Very well. Then it is mine.’ [25]
episodes.worst: [10]–[22]: three quotes, a temple name said twice and a two-sentence Sabi summary between the deathbed and Chunchu’s decision.
fixes: Give the dying emperor one line on the page before [1]’s death (Saluzi, or his own name to his son), so his exit lands.
Cut [12] or [11] (the temple name twice) and the retelling quotes [13] or [14], [18] and [32].
Play this episode before #49, and either dramatize Sabi [19]–[22] in three lines of dialogue or cut it.

episodes.title: King Muyeol
episodes.verdict: The arc’s biggest payoff, Chunchu taking the chair he has avoided since #2, is a summary sentence and a chorus of anonymous emoji speakers; dramatize Alchun being offered the crown and handing it to Chunchu.
episodes.romance: Munhee and Chunchu get one beat [17]–[19], a marriage rather than a romance; the dream-for-a-skirt callback to #14 lands (‘In hindsight she undercharged’).
episodes.best: Munhee: ‘My sister sold me that dream for one silk skirt. In hindsight she undercharged.’ [19]
episodes.worst: [8]–[15]: the coronation as summary, an unattributed quote and anonymous emoji lines.
fixes: Dramatize the succession: the council offers Alchun the crown (firing #44 [81]); he laughs and names Chunchu, speaking the [11] words as dialogue. Cut the quote.
Replace the emoji speakers [12]–[15], [21]–[23] with named people, and tag [22] as the king.
Tell the end of Sacred Bone once: keep Kangrim [3]–[6]; cut [7] and [24].

episodes.title: Jahee
episodes.verdict: Either grow this into a real romance with an obstacle and a cost and bring Jahee back later, or fold it into Bupmin’s next scene as a flashback; as a standalone it is a sketch that stalls the war.
episodes.romance: A sketch, not a romance. Desire is there (he watches her mouth [7]) and so is chemistry in the first exchange (‘Count again. / While I am watching.’ [5]; his ‘Please show me’ [6]). But there is no obstacle beyond a coughing father, the escalation from correction to kiss takes one paragraph [8], nobody chooses anything that costs, and the payoff is a record [12]. ‘Years later the court will name her Jayi’ [11] promises a future she never gets: Jahee never appears again in the book. We like her; we get no time to root for them.
episodes.best: Jahee: ‘Your sums are wrong. / The tide does not care that you are a prince. / Count again.’ [5]
episodes.worst: [13]–[16]: a time-skip summary and a ‘king for all’ exchange that belongs to a different episode.
fixes: Open on Jahee’s ‘Your sums are wrong.’ [5] and fold [0] into a later line.

Give the romance an obstacle and a cost (rank: a True Bone prince and a clerk’s daughter; or his recall to the yard) and play the kiss over a few exchanges. Cut the shot-list fragments [7] and the caption lines [9].
Pay her off: bring Jahee back when Bupmin is crowned or goes to war (she never reappears), or move this episode to its year and let Bupmin’s later scenes carry her.

episodes.title: Hyukgose
episodes.verdict: Open on the six chiefs creeping at the winged horse, cut the four summaries and the unattributed manifesto, and name the surname Park so the three myths add up.
episodes.romance: Hyukgose and Alyoung: told in one sentence (‘They marry because they want each other. The omens agree.’ [15]), echoed by the same line twice [26], [28]. Her card promises friction (‘the one person in Seorabeol who can tell the king no’ [16]) and the text never plays it.
episodes.best: The chiefs creeping at the horse: ‘You ever seen a horse with wings? I haven’t. / …That one’s got wings, though.’ [8]
episodes.worst: [0]–[5] and [19]–[27]: the egg told four times before its scene, then an unattributed manifesto and a name table.
fixes: Give the manifesto [21]–[24] to Alpyung as dialogue; cut ‘Why did Old Joseon fall?’ [20] and the name table [27].
Name the surname Park (from the gourd-shaped egg) so the triad pays off as Park, Seok and Kim, and spell the city Surabol as #51, #52 and #55 do, not Seorabeol.

episodes.title: Talhae
episodes.verdict: Nearly there: cut three of the five quotes that restate the paragraph before them, and it is the best standalone in the slice.
episodes.battle: The Talhae–Suro shapeshift duel [6]–[9] is a one-paragraph mini-battle with a clear prize (the throne), an escalation (hawk against eagle, sparrow against falcon) and a funny concession (‘That was a falcon. / Fine. I’ll find a country with a smaller king.’). Short, played, good.
episodes.best: Hogong: ‘…You buried those last night.’ / Talhae: ‘Prove it.’ [24]–[25]
episodes.worst: The five quotes [2], [15], [19], [26], [30], which stop a comedy five times to repeat it.
fixes: Cut quotes [2], [15] and [26].
Gloss ‘Wa’ once at [1].
At [27] (‘every king of Silla lives in a stolen house’), add a half-line that lands on the present: including the one who sits there now.

episodes.title: Alji
episodes.verdict: Cut two of the three quotes and say plainly that this boy’s line leads to Chunchu, so the myth triad lands on the arc’s hero.
episodes.best: Talhae: ‘Well. / I came in a box too, you know. Mine was bigger.’ [6]
episodes.worst: [7]–[9]: quote, naming, quote.
fixes: Cut two of the three quotes [4], [7], [9].
Make the Kim link explicit at [10]: this boy’s line leads to Chunchu.
Name the steam’s word at [11] (Kim), and close on the present before the Baekje card.

episodes.title: Exile
episodes.verdict: The scenes are strong (the clan pact, the name offer, the island), but the episode tells the exile three times and out of order; tell it once, in sequence, and open on the three-year hook.
episodes.battle: [6] is legend, not battle: Gyebek’s one-horse run at the enemy general (‘does not finish turning’) is vivid, plants Gomanari and the reverse grip, and pays off at #72.
episodes.best: [34]–[36] ‘The king made that one up.’ / ‘Yes. Which is why it is owed to someone.’
episodes.worst: [44]–[57]: the exile retold, Minister Satek naming himself, then a record of a different exile.
fixes: Put it in causal order and tell the exile once: mourning [2] → clan pact [11]–[31] → offer [33]–[36] → arrow [39]–[43] → sealed order and boat [49]–[56]. Cut [9]–[10], [38], [44], [57].
Open on [2] and fold [0] into it.
Give Euija a real scene at [77]–[80]: he finds his own seal on the order and decides something specific about Gyebek that #64 must answer.

episodes.title: Heaven–Earth King
episodes.verdict: The best myth in the slice and a complete standalone tale; just give each twin one name in English.
episodes.romance: Not a romance. The god’s stay with the Lady of Wisdom is one line [32]; her ‘I’ll be here. I’ll have rice on.’ [49] is the tender beat. Right weight for a myth.
episodes.best: [27]–[28] ‘There’s nobody under heaven who can touch me.’ / ‘That’s why I came from above.’
episodes.worst: [3] and [87]–[89]: a chant and re-shown cards around the edges, plus the doubled twin names.
fixes: One name per twin in English.
Cut the opening chant [3] and the repeated cards [88]–[89].
Fix the card [108]: Yuri Dora is ‘he’, and Gyebek is mending the roof, not hiding on it.

episodes.title: Sulmun
episodes.verdict: Gyebek’s questions are the episode; cut the second record and give the porridge tragedy one reaction.
episodes.best: [6]–[8] ‘Was there a hole in the apron.’ / ‘…How did you know that?’
episodes.worst: [14]–[16]: two records around a two-sentence tale.
fixes: Cut record [16].
Add one Gyebek reaction to the porridge tragedy [12]–[13].
If ‘one short’ is meant for Yellow Mountain, let Gyebek recall it there; otherwise cut the MORAL [20].

episodes.title: Three Princes
episodes.verdict: The title tale is a telegram plus two records; the episode lives in the diver’s kindness, the ox divorce and ‘Tell that part again’.
episodes.romance: Baekjuto and Socheon-guk [24]–[32] is a marriage played as a comedy of appetite (‘…I also ate someone else’s.’). Quick and funny; it’s a divorce, not a romance.
episodes.best: [35]–[37] ‘Tell that part again.’ / ‘Which part.’ / ‘The part where he comes home.’
episodes.worst: [2]–[15]: the title tale in summary, telegram lines and two records.
fixes: Cut records [14]–[15] and the telegram lines [7]–[12].
Build the episode on the diver scene and the son who comes home.
Fold #63’s single point (why Tamla takes Baekje’s exiles) into [16] and delete #63.

episodes.title: Stone Lady
episodes.verdict: An anthology told in summary; keep Gameunjang, fix the serpent quote and the mislabeled husband.
episodes.romance: Sanbangduk [10]–[14]: one good exchange (‘when I hold your hand I don’t feel like stone’), then the murder and her return in two sentences. Told, not played; too thin to move anyone.
episodes.best: [29]–[30] ‘So the child they threw away was the luck.’ / ‘No. The luck was always hers.’
episodes.worst: [5]–[8]: the serpent tale, where the record contradicts the narration.
fixes: Cut the serpent record [8] (or the whole serpent tale).
Relabel [13] as the husband.
Cut the MORALs [19] and [32]; Gyebek’s lines already make the point.

episodes.title: Gardener
episodes.verdict: Two good tales with real dialogue; play Jacheongbi’s loss and her lover’s return instead of summarizing them in a line each.
episodes.romance: Jacheongbi and Mun Doryeong [26]–[39] is the best-played short romance in the slice: desire (three years at one desk), an obstacle (no women allowed), chemistry (‘…I had no eyes.’ / ‘You have them now.’) and a reveal that costs her. Then the cost [33] and the payoff [39] are told in a line each. We root for her and are denied the scene.
episodes.best: [40]–[42] ‘…Can the dead be fetched back.’ / ‘In stories.’ / ‘…I see.’
episodes.worst: [33]–[39]: the romance’s death and resurrection in summary.
fixes: Play Mun Doryeong’s death and revival as short scenes.
Cut record [12] and the empty MORAL [17].
If the loophole Gyebek ‘asks to hear twice’ [25] matters, let him use one later; otherwise cut [43].

episodes.title: Kangrim
episodes.verdict: The origin pays off big at #72, but [2] and [10] compress a murder case into a blur; play the descent and the crow and cut the rest.
episodes.best: [20] ‘…Then a man can die before his king, and the book still opens.’
episodes.worst: [2] and [10]: the murder case nobody can follow.
fixes: Rewrite [2] as three plain sentences; set up or cut ‘the couple’ [10].
Cut Dongbangsak [18] to one line and drop Haewonmek’s name here.
Re-aim the card [23] at Sabi.

episodes.title: Tribute
episodes.verdict: A 177-word footnote that restates #59 [16]; fold its one good line into #59 and delete it.
episodes.best: [0] ‘Rebellion would at least have been legible; this is closer to forgetting.’
episodes.worst: [2]–[4]: a record and its restatement.
fixes: Delete #63 and move one line into #59 [16].
Point #62’s card at Sabi.

episodes.title: Coup
episodes.verdict: Sharp satire and a great plant (Ye Sikjin’s drawer), but interrupt the speech, stage the mole’s reveal, and mention Gyebek, the reason for the coup.
episodes.romance: The maids [33]–[37] are seduction, not romance, and ‘As you did for General Gyebek — take your time.’ stings: he once named a soldier, now he names concubines.
episodes.battle: A political battle with clear stakes, a POV and a reversal (‘He has already changed who is sitting.’ [25]), but the moves are summarized after the fact. Dramatize Chunbok’s sleeve going up.
episodes.best: [10] ‘Also he printed the proclamation before the session. I can smell the ink.’
episodes.worst: [3]–[8]: the uninterrupted proclamation.
fixes: Cut the proclamation [3]–[8] to two blocks and cross-cut the room.
Add the Gyebek beat (a recall written and not sent).
Stage Chunbok’s turn in the Assembly instead of summarizing it [25]–[30]; cut record [19].

episodes.title: Descent
episodes.verdict: Cut the thirteen shot-list paragraphs [14]–[26]; what remains (the nightmares, ‘That… who?’, Seongchung’s death) is a strong episode.
episodes.romance: No romance; the banquet is a harem montage. The maids’ banter [27]–[35] has real wit (‘Then Your Majesty still has room to work with.’) and could carry the decadence on its own.
episodes.best: [36] ‘He laughs for the first time in four months. It is the last recorded instance.’
episodes.worst: [14]–[26]: thirteen paragraphs of shot-list narration.
fixes: Cut [14]–[26] to one paragraph.
Make Seongchung’s arrest clear at [51], cut record [52], and unify Seongchung/Sungchung.
Give Heungsu one live line before his exile [8] and drop the ‘hollow ring’ fragments.

episodes.title: Nine Omens
episodes.verdict: This is where Euija’s whole story pays off; tell the omens once and it is the slice’s best history episode after #69.
episodes.best: [12.2] ‘He made them himself. Which makes him the worst reader of signs alive.’
episodes.worst: [2]–[11]: the omens told twice before the shaman tells them again.
fixes: Cut the omen list [2]–[10] (or the widget [11]).
Open on [1], not [0].
Fix [38] (‘sent away’) and [29] (‘took the throne’).

episodes.title: Onjo
episodes.verdict: A warm payoff for the Jumong arc, but it yanks the reader away right after ‘Summon Gyebek…!’, and its last-night scene re-runs #39’s lines.
episodes.romance: Jumong and Sosuno [19]–[38] have real chemistry in the banter (‘That’s… a lot of buckets for one road.’ / ‘Not buckets. Grain. Boys. Me.’), a choice that costs (‘I’m not sitting in a footnote.’) and a tender exit (‘Keep the well. I’m taking the glow.’). [29] promises ‘Older. Hungrier.’, but [31]–[33] replays #39 [176]/[178] almost word for word (‘man meat’, ‘Beat up Little Sosuno’), so the farewell night reads as a rerun. Something new between them would make it count.
episodes.best: [49] ‘Your father crossed a river on turtles’ backs. A deer’s practically civilised.’
episodes.worst: [31]–[33]: the explicit exchange recycled from #39, plus the [41] spoiler and two records.
fixes: Move #67 out of the gap after ‘Summon Gyebek…!’ (before #64 works), or cut it to the stag and the naming.
Write a new last-night exchange instead of reusing #39’s lines.

episodes.title: Sungchung
episodes.verdict: A 208-word stub named for a man who died two episodes ago; merge it into #69.
episodes.battle: Pre-battle: ‘Who is the Eraha of this country?!’ [5] has heat, and Ye Sikjin’s sum [6] is the sharpest line about stakes. No plan is shown.
episodes.best: [6] ‘And how many from the capital to his own gate?’
episodes.worst: [0]–[3]: summary, a record and an aphorism.
fixes: Merge #68 into #69 as its opening scene.
Settle where Gyebek is when Chunbok objects [4].

episodes.title: Heungsu
episodes.verdict: The best history episode in the slice; fix the impossible ‘655 berth’ flashback and give Euija a reason for ‘So it is’.
episodes.battle: The best pre-battle geography in the book. The yard map (the river mouth drawn twice as wide, one notch for the pass) teaches the reader the two doors [2.1] before #72 uses them, and ‘You’re standing on Tanhyeon.’ [10] makes the stakes physical.
episodes.best: [10] ‘You’re standing on Tanhyeon.’
episodes.worst: [1]: the berth flashback that breaks the timeline.
fixes: Re-date or rewrite the berth flashback [1].
Dramatize the ministers’ counter-plan [14] and give Euija a reason.
Use one name for the pass.

episodes.title: Gyebek
episodes.verdict: The defining act of Gyebek’s life happens to a family the reader has never met, in one record; plant them, and plant the vow #72 calls back.
episodes.battle: None yet; the march sets the stakes (‘the last latch on the road to Sabi’ [24]).
episodes.best: [21] ‘A horse can’t be made a slave. / A horse is just a horse.’
episodes.worst: [16]–[17]: the family killing as a footnote.
fixes: Plant the family in #56 and on the island; keep the act offstage but show the yard first.
Have Gyebek speak the vow here (‘I will complete my duty’) so #72’s callback has a source.
Let him recall Euija’s ‘Judge it yourself’ (#29 [11]) when he decides.

episodes.title: Three Realms
episodes.verdict: A god sitcom labelled ‘Epilogue’ and parked between the march and the battle; move or cut it, and pay off Kangrim’s question or drop it.
episodes.romance: Samsin and Haemosu [12]–[17] flirt about appetite. It’s banter, not a romance, and it touches no mortal story.
episodes.best: [37] ‘Let the meeting begin. / Business of the living… last item on the agenda.’
episodes.worst: [4]–[20]: servant gossip at the doorstep of the battle.
fixes: Move #71 out of the gap between #70 and #72.
Cut the gossip [4]–[20] to three lines; remove the stage directions and the ‘Epilogue · Part II’ label.
Pay off Kangrim’s question or cut it.

episodes.title: Yellow Mountain
episodes.verdict: The four clashes, the parley and Gwanchang make this the best episode in the slice. But the first third belongs to the Red Fowl, a widget announces the result before the fight, and Gyebek's last line pays off a vow the reader never heard while Euija is absent.
episodes.battle: A real battle, and in its middle a very good one. Stakes are clear: this field is 'that door' to Sabi [43], and Silla has a date [11], [17]. The geography is easy to follow: three camps, three roads, 'no fourth way in' [28]. The plan and its reversals work clash by clash. The left camp had been shooting half its arrows [53], the right camp moved forty paces in the night [58], [70], and Yushin is cut in the fourth [61]. Kangrim visible to all five thousand, who cheer him [37]–[39], is an unforgettable image. The count 'One… Four' and 'nobody says five' [112] is a superb device. The parley [67]–[87] is the best dialogue in the slice, and Gwanchang [95]–[108] gives the cost a face; a father's wet sleeve turns the battle [110]–[111]. Three things weaken it. The outcome is announced at [33] and pre-spent at [26] and [88]. Baekje's losses have no face: the only Baekje voice besides Gyebek is unnamed, so 'Four. Now.' [79] is arithmetic, not grief. And the duel is summarized [61] while the death drifts into lore [116]–[119].
episodes.best: 'Four. Now.' / 'I know. I can count too.' / 'Then go home.' / 'You first.' [79]–[82]; and 'On the Baekje side, nobody says five.' [112]
episodes.worst: [113]–[124]. The last minute of the last stand is split between a duplicated weather sentence, a Kangrim-origin exchange that contradicts #62, and a flashback to a vow #4 never contained. It belongs to lore instead of to Gyebek and Euija.
fixes: Rebuild the death on what the reader actually saw. In [120], replay #4 [111.8]–[111.11] ('Do you like the name, or do you like me?' … 'Yes.'). Have Kangrim ask the question #29 [11] planted: 'He told you to judge his orders yourself. Did you?' Cut [117]–[119] to one line of origin.

Clear the runway. Trim the Red Fowl cold open [1]–[5] to a card. Move the FORMATION spoiler [33] to the end. Cut [26], [42], [44], [64]–[65], [88] and [107]. Spend the room on the duel at [61], played in five beats with the reverse grip from #56 [6].

Give the cost a Baekje face and a mirror. Name the adjutant of [34]–[36] and [56], and let him be one of the names that stop answering at [113]. At [106], tie Gwanchang's face to the children Gyebek killed in #70.

episodes.title: Sabi
episodes.verdict: The Ye Sikjin betrayal is the best-built mini-story in the slice. Around it, the episode skips Euija's reaction to Gyebek's death, cuts away from every big confrontation after a few lines, and stops dead for seven quotes in a row.
episodes.romance: The only intimate thread is the two Court Maids, at Euija's side since #4 [7]. Their last beat [58]–[59] ('He isn't here today. …But the body remembers.') could be a haunting end to that relationship. Stranded after the quote pile, it reads as a stray line. Move it to the cliff.
episodes.battle: No battle is shown. Sabi falls by surrender, which fits history and the book's theme of doors opened from inside, and Yushin's axe in the Red Fowl's tent [8]–[13] supplies the confrontation, with a good comic button in Dong Baoliang stepping on his commander's foot [11].
